public static final Supplier<TwilightCloakItem> TWILIGHT_CLOAK = ITEMS.register("twilight_cloak", TwilightCloakItem::new);

rows.concrete_observation: Native registered cloak constructor installs LivingChangeTarget and EntityTick.Pre listeners. shouldResetTarget requires target is Player, enabled exact cloak anywhere in InventoryHelper provider handlers, and target local max raw brightness<=configured threshold(default4 range0..15). It does not require INVISIBILITY effect or its successful application, cloak armor slot, sneaking, source enemy class, player not attacking, cooldown, attacker ownership or sight. New about-to-be target matching this policy cancels change event. Pre-tick Mob whose current target matches policy calls resetTarget: clear five predefined Brain memories if present and setTarget(null); default overload resetRevengeTarget=false therefore lastHurtByMob remains. Both are one admission/maintenance policy, not two implementations. Separately normal inventory tick excludes client/nonplayer/spectator, updateInvisibility checks enabled/light and unconditionally attempts two-tick hidden INVISIBILITY, ignoring admission. Worn tick calls same helper with Player cast and lacks these shown inventory guards; actual accessory dispatch not expanded. Toggle use only server+shift changes enabled component and emits XP pickup sound; glint reflects enabled, not actual light eligibility, accepted effect or actual AI refusal. No denied-target receipt is emitted by either AI handler. Event handlers have no explicit server filter in this source, unlike normal inventory tick.
rows.application_to_boss_immune: AI rejection can be a direct policy independent of visual potion admission; no invisibility icon or glint proves accepted control or combat immunity. For a Boss control receipt distinguish new-target admission from old-target cleanup and surviving revenge memory, and attach any message to actual decision rather than generic toggle sound. This example protects target selection, not final hurt, so cannot prove damage immunity or solve guard final damage boundary alone.
rows.semantic_dedup: One candidate for enabled inventory+actual ambient light target refusal/maintenance, not two for event/tick or five for memory keys. Prior Reliquary mob charm is entity-ID ingredient resource/cache targeting with post-kill charm damage; this has no charm entity whitelist/budget and explicitly shares condition with a separate failed-admission-agnostic invisibility producer. Master Wizardry forcefield is spatial cross-membership attack event, not this light/exact-item target policy. Compare fear/mindcontrol targets without treating null target wrapper as credit. Russell final semantic review required; all helper credit0.
rows.limitations: Static source only. No proof event engine behavior preserves previous target on cancellation, all modded memory/AI paths included, eventual retarget rate, final attacks blocked, or user actually invisible. No source-side per-target throttle, immune text, UUID payload or sound on refusal. Config declaration read but runtime configuration unknown. Curios dispatch and game runtime not executed.

exclusions: All target and memory cleanup adapters merge one policy; memory constants, two-tick effect, glint and toggle XP sound earn no independent credit.
